# vNext runtime feature matrix

Snapshot of the machine-readable runtime metadata (`@burgan-tech/vnext-meta` **0.0.53**). Known runtime version: **0.0.100**, matching schema version: **0.0.56**.

How to read it: a workspace whose `vnext.config.json` `runtimeVersion` is **older** than a row's `since` does not have that feature. Anything the toolkit references (skills, references) that is newer than the workspace runtime must be treated as unavailable there. The hand-written references under `references/concepts/` explain *how* to use each feature; this file only answers *since when* and *is it still there*.

## Known issues

| Id | Affected | Fixed in | Severity | Component | Title | Workaround |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `automatic-transition-chain-depth-capped` | >=0.0.26 | open | error | transition | Automatic transition sync dispatch stops when chain depth exceeds 50; the pipeline fails with error code Transition:100017. | Refactor the workflow so automatic chains do not exceed the depth guard, insert intermediate human states, or split logic across transitions. |
| `scheduled-transition-without-timer-skipped` | >=0.0.26 | open | warning | timer | If a scheduled transition has no timer configuration, ScheduleTransitionsStep logs a warning and skips enqueueing that schedule (transition does not fire from scheduling). | Ensure every scheduled transition defines a timer evaluated by the timer service. |
| `workflow-timeout-mapping-fallback-static-duration` | >=0.0.26 | open | warning | timer | When dynamic workflow timeout mapping fails, the runtime falls back to the static ISO 8601 duration from workflow timeout configuration. | Fix or simplify the timeout mapping script; verify TimeoutMappingFallback logs during instance start. |
| `workflow-timeout-job-scheduling-failure-non-blocking` | >=0.0.26 | open | warning | instance | If enqueueing or persisting the workflow timeout background job throws, the failure is logged but instance start continues without blocking. | Monitor WorkflowTimeoutSchedulingFailed logs and job infrastructure; retry or reconcile timeouts externally if needed. |
| `cancel-scheduled-jobs-failure-does-not-block-transition` | >=0.0.26 | open | warning | timer | When cancelling scheduled transition jobs for the leaving state fails, the pipeline logs ScheduledJobsCancellationFailed and continues the transition anyway. | Inspect cancellation/job-store failures; manually reconcile orphaned scheduled jobs if transitions completed despite cancellation errors. |
| `async-transition-enqueue-lock-race-silent-loss` | >=0.0.26 <0.0.69 | 0.0.69 | error | transition | Async (sync=false) transition jobs could fire while the enqueue-side distributed lock still held the same instance key; the job consumer failed with a lock conflict that was silently swallowed, losing the transition and stranding the instance in Busy status. | Retry the transition after the instance is recovered; upgrade to a fixed version where the enqueue lock is scoped with an :enqueue suffix and the job handler retries lock conflicts and faults the instance on exhaustion. |
| `duplicate-async-transition-job-conflict` | >=0.0.26 | open | info | transition | A second async transition request for the same instance and transition key while a job is already active is rejected with HTTP 409 Conflict. | Use idempotency keys, poll instance state, or wait for the in-flight job to finish before retrying. |
| `instance-data-numeric-precision-loss` | <=0.0.85 | open | warning | instance | Instance data appends reformat every number through int/double, so integers above 2^53 (including values that no longer fit int64) and decimals beyond ~15 significant digits are persisted with reduced precision — and the rewrite touches numbers the append never referenced. | Set WorkflowExecution:InstanceDataWrite:PreserveNumericPrecision=true to canonicalize numbers losslessly (int64 exact, decimal in plain notation; values beyond decimal's 28-29 significant digits are still rounded). |
| `enqueue-relay-drops-subflow-chain-reserve-claim` | >=0.0.80 <=0.0.93 | 0.0.94 | error | execution | The internal enqueue relay's event-to-payload copy omitted SubflowChainReserved, so with WorkflowExecution:DirectEnqueueContinuations=false (or when the direct Dapr enqueue falls back to the outbox) an async transition on a parent with an active SubFlow reached the leaf without the chain-reserve claim its own accept had taken, and the leaf rejected the forward as Busy (Instance:100031). | Keep DirectEnqueueContinuations=true (the default); the drop then only bites when the direct Dapr enqueue fails and the outbox fallback carries a subflow-forward transition. |
| `arming-poller-not-hosted-orphans-arm-failures` | <=0.0.92 | open | error | background-jobs | The Aether arming poller is registered only by the Orchestration host and switched off there (WithHostedService=false, also in the vnext-runtime deployment templates), so no process arms recovery. When the immediate Dapr scheduler arm fails (scheduler restart/outage at accept, timer arm, ack-timeout arm), Aether rolls the job row back to Pending 'for the arming poller' - and nothing ever arms it. The async accept has already answered 202 and reserved the instance, so the instance stays Busy forever; retries are rejected by the Busy check and the duplicate-active-job guard. Verified live (issue #935 chaos test): a Pending row sat unarmed for 15 minutes with the scheduler healthy again; enabling the poller recovered it within seconds. | Set BackgroundJob:WithHostedService=true on exactly one host (orchestration) so the arming poller and reapers run. |
| `past-due-oneshot-arm-race-orphans-scheduled-row` | <=0.0.92 | open | error | background-jobs | Arming a past-due one-shot races the Dapr scheduler's immediate fire: the job callback can arrive before the armer commits Pending->Scheduled, JobDispatcher answers 'not found in an active state; skipping' with HTTP 200, Dapr deletes the consumed one-shot, and the armer then commits Scheduled - leaving a Scheduled row with no scheduler entry, permanently. The VisibilityTimeout reaper covers Running rows only, so nothing recovers it. Observed live (issue #935 chaos test, outbox mode + poller on): dispatcher skip at 12:17:38Z, row Scheduled for 11+ minutes, instance Busy. Aether-level defect; the same orphan also results from a failed rollback after a direct-arm timeout whose server-side registration succeeded. | Manual: set the orphaned sys_queues.BackgroundJobs row Status back to 5 (Pending) so the poller re-arms it (Dapr one-shot arming is overwrite-idempotent). |
| `discovery-domain-list-single-page-ceiling` | >=0.0.94 | open | warning | runtime | The registry's domain-list function serves a single page (500 rows today) and its response carries no truncation signal, so a registry holding more domains than that warms only the first 500. | The runtime logs WorkflowLogs 50038 DomainListCeilingReached at Warning when the list comes back at or above ServiceDiscovery:Cache:DomainListExpectedMax, and publishes it anyway - the domains beyond the ceiling are simply not warmed and each pays a live per-domain lookup, which is the behaviour with the cache switched off. |
| `workflow-timeout-reset-not-implemented` | >=0.0.1 | open | warning | runtime | timer.reset is required by the schema but is read NOWHERE in the runtime, so a workflow timeout always means 'not finished within duration, counted from instance start' and never 'idle for duration'. Whatever the field says - 'never', 'OnEntry' - the behaviour is identical. | Author the duration as an absolute budget from start and do not rely on activity resetting it; every authored value in the reference corpus today declares OnEntry against a runtime that ignores it. |
| `state-level-subprocess-rejected-at-publish` | >=0.0.95 | open | error | workflow | A state starts a SubFlow and only a SubFlow: state.subFlow.type must be 'S'. A SubProcess is started by its own task (SubProcessTask, TaskType.SubProcess = 14), which creates the correlation itself, not by a state. WorkflowValidator now rejects a state-level subFlow.type of 'P' at publish. This is not a regression: the shape never worked on the sync path - it returned 409 Instance:100031 and left the parent Busy and not Faulted with no automatic recovery - and only appeared to work when driven asynchronously, where a job re-entry happened to carry IsPreReserved. | Model the SubProcess as a SubProcessTask on a transition or state hook instead of as state.subFlow, keeping the child workflow itself unchanged. |
| `pre-reserved-job-failure-can-strand-busy` | >=0.0.26 | open | error | transition | An async accept flips Busy before answering 202, and a job re-entry that fails with a non-lock-conflict Result error (for example a policy re-validation failure) logs JobFailed and returns without faulting, so that Busy can be left with no owner - the pipeline's own fault path covers only failures inside the step loop, retry requires Faulted, and the sync path leaves no job row for recovery. Note that a blanket "fault on any job failure" is not the fix: it faults a parent that is legitimately Busy for its subflow child's lifetime, which was measured to break a working chain (ChainBusy.PostCommitForwardFailure_ReleasesTheChainReserve_SoNoLevelStaysBusy, root left Faulted in root-waiting with a JOB_EXECUTION_FAILED incident). A correct fix needs a predicate for "this execution owns that Busy", which the job handler does not have today. | Recover a stranded instance manually with cancel/exit; prefer sync for transitions whose policy may change between accept and re-entry. |
| `function-multi-task-taskresponse-slot-collision` | >=0.0.26 <=0.0.94 | 0.0.95 | error | function | In a function with multiple onExecutionTasks, every ScriptContext.TaskResponse slot carried the LAST executed task's payload: SetStandardResponse aliased each response tree into the shared Body, and the in-place expando merge of the next task's response rewrote the earlier slots. Output scripts reading TaskResponse composed the wrong response; OutputResponse slots (re-serialized snapshots) were unaffected. | Read task results from ScriptContext.OutputResponse[variableName] instead of TaskResponse, or publish the function with a single task. |
| `masked-field-same-version-republish-stale-etag` | >=0.0.99 | open | warning | schema | Re-publishing a master schema at the same version with changed x-masking (or x-roles) does not move the data-function ETag; clients holding a body keep it (304) until the instance data changes or the cache entry expires. | Bump the schema version whenever x-masking or x-roles changes. |
| `list-filter-probes-guarded-fields` | >=0.0.79 | open | warning | query | Instance list filters, sorting and groupBy run on the raw JSONB value, so a caller can probe an x-roles-hidden field through them. x-masking cannot be combined with x-filterOperators/x-sortable (rejected at publish), but the x-roles case is pre-existing. | Do not declare x-filterOperators or x-sortable on fields guarded by x-roles; set Workflow:InstanceFiltering:EnforceMasterSchemaFiltering=true so only declared fields are filterable. |
| `field-hash-low-entropy-values` | >=0.0.99 | open | warning | schema | x-encryption hash is pseudonymisation, not anonymisation: low-entropy values (national ids, phone numbers) can be brute-forced by anyone who can read the instance's salt from InstanceSecrets. | Restrict database access; use x-roles to hide values that must not be matchable at all. |
| `field-encryption-plaintext-copies` | >=0.0.99 | open | high | runtime | x-encryption 'encrypt' covers InstancesData only: InstanceTransition.Body/Header, InstanceTask.Request/Response/InvocationResult, outbox InstanceSubCompleted/Faulted payloads, job payloads and the human-task cache still hold the plaintext | Treat encrypt as InstanceData field encryption, not 'PII encrypted at rest'. |
| `field-encryption-lazy-history` | >=0.0.99 | open | medium | runtime | Rows written before a field became x-encryption 'encrypt' stay plaintext (append-only history, lazy migration); new rows are encrypted | A backfill tool is Phase 2. |
| `field-encryption-script-key-access` | >=0.0.99 | open | high | runtime | The per-instance x-encryption key and salt are stored in plaintext in the flow schema's InstanceSecrets table next to the data they protect; a database reader (or a script with raw database access) can decrypt every encrypt value | Accepted (requester decision): database security is owned by the DB team and the runtime never serves the secrets. |
| `field-encryption-rollback-floor` | >=0.0.99 | open | medium | runtime | A runtime older than 0.0.99 cannot open x-encryption tokens and would hand them to the engine as values | Publish the first encrypt/hash schema only after every orchestration pod runs >= 0.0.99 and its migration (InstanceSecrets) is applied; roll back with SchemaEncryption__EncryptWrites=false rather than a binary downgrade. |
| `field-encryption-selector-unguarded` | >=0.0.99 | open | medium | runtime | Event selectors (FindByFilterAsync) carry no schema context and are not refused on an x-encryption 'encrypt' path; they match ciphertext and silently find nothing | Never select on an encrypted field in an event mapping or selector. |
| `field-encryption-same-instance-token-swap` | >=0.0.99 | open | low | runtime | x-encryption tokens are bound to scheme, instance and path but not to the row, so a database writer could swap tokens between versions of the same instance and path without detection | Accepted: it keeps unchanged values' tokens stable, echo possible and rollback safe. |
| `field-encryption-job-deferral` | >=0.0.99 | open | low | runtime | A write that would carry an unopenable x-encryption encrypt value forward (its InstanceSecrets row deleted outside the runtime, or the token tampered) is refused with Instance:100040 at the write, so the transition fails at the step that writes instead of being refused before admission; reads keep serving the token | The runtime deletes a secret row only together with its instance. |
| `field-hash-no-cross-instance-matching` | >=0.0.99 | open | info | schema | x-encryption hash digests use a per-instance salt, so the same value hashes differently in two instances; digests cannot be joined or deduplicated across instances | By design. |
| `field-encryption-shred-l1-delay` | >=0.0.99 | open | low | runtime | Deleting an instance's InstanceSecrets row (crypto-shredding) takes effect on a pod only once its in-process L1 entry is gone (sliding SchemaEncryption:SecretCacheSlidingMinutes, default 30, or a restart); until then that pod keeps opening the values | After shredding, wait out the sliding window or restart the orchestration pods. |
| `cacheaside-source-mapping-input-ignored` | >=0.0.71 <=0.0.98 | 0.0.99 | error | task | CacheAsideTask ran its source task without the source mapping's InputHandler: sourceMapping was applied only as output shaping over the cached raw source result, so a source that needs its configuration set by a mapping (for example GetInstanceData SetKey, an HTTP URL or body) ran unconfigured, and the cache held the raw payload instead of the shaped value. | Upgrade to 0.0.99, where the source runs as a task with sourceMapping as its mapping (InputHandler -> invoke -> OutputHandler) and the shaped output is cached. |
| `task-binding-x-request-id-dropped` | >=0.0.80 <=0.0.98 | 0.0.99 | error | task | Task invokers treated X-Request-Id as a reserved trace header: a value set in the task's headers or input mapping was silently dropped from the outbound call and no value was sent in its place, so APIs that require it (OHVPS/BKM) rejected the call with 400 TR.OHVPS.Resource.InvalidFormat. StartTrigger and SubProcess never dropped the mapping's value but did not send vNext's request id either. | Upgrade to 0.0.99, where a non-empty X-Request-Id from the input mapping is sent as is and, when the mapping sets none, vNext's own request id (the originating request's X-Request-Id) is sent — on every HTTP-shaped task type, StartTrigger and SubProcess included. |
| `long-poll-non-terminating-interaction-suppressed` | >=0.0.95 <=0.0.97 | 0.0.98 | warning | state | The state function stopped emitting the interaction block for a state declaring interaction.longPoll.terminate: false. The outstanding-ack presence condition introduced in 0.0.95 was applied to every long poll, but only a terminating state arms an acknowledge token, so a non-terminating state's block (terminateLongPoll: false + fallbackTimeoutSeconds) was suppressed entirely and the client never learned the declared long-poll window. | Upgrade to 0.0.98, where a non-terminating state's block is served whenever the instance is in it and the caller passes the gate, without an ack href (StateFunctionCache ResponseShapeVersion v13). |
| `script-context-incident-not-loaded` | >=0.0.93 <=0.0.98 | 0.0.99 | error | script | A script reading context.Incident saw HasActiveIncident = true but ActiveIncident = null and TotalIncidentCount = 0, including a mapping running inside error-boundary handling of a subflow fault. ScriptIncidentInfo read the EF navigation, which is always empty on the script context's instance snapshot (loaded incidents are detached there). The upward InstanceSubFaultedEvent payload had the same navigation-only read and dropped an incident loaded no-tracking. | Upgrade to 0.0.99, where ScriptIncidentInfo and the upward fault payload read the loaded incidents. |
| `async-transition-oversized-body-stuck-busy` | >=0.0.26 <=0.0.98 | 0.0.99 | error | transition | An async (sync=false) transition whose request body exceeds the Dapr scheduler's message ceiling (etcd, 2 MiB default) was accepted with 202 but refused at arm time — after the Busy flip and the job row had committed — leaving the instance durably Busy with no transition record, no incident and no recovery path; the oversized job could also stop the dapr-scheduler for every domain until a restart, losing armed jobs. | Keep async transition bodies well under 2 MiB (upload files to a document store and pass references). |
| `sandbox-baseline-missing-system-objectmodel` | >=0.0.26 <=0.0.98 | 0.0.99 | error | runtime | With the script sandbox enabled, the shipped AllowedAssemblies baseline lacked System.ObjectModel, so a mapping that enumerates an ExpandoObject (foreach — ordinary mapping code) failed to compile with CS0012 (ExpandoObject implements INotifyPropertyChanged, which lives in System.ObjectModel; the netstandard facade's type-forward does not satisfy the binder). Direct System.ObjectModel types (ObservableCollection) failed with CS1069. Plain is/cast/dynamic access compiled — the failure was construct-dependent. | Add "System.ObjectModel" to Scripting:Sandbox:AllowedAssemblies in the environment's configuration, grant it per mapping via scripts.allowedAssemblies, or read the expando through the 'as IDictionary<string,object>' spelling without enumerating the expando itself. |
| `role-grant-combinators-rollback-floor` | >=0.0.99 | open | medium | runtime | A runtime older than 0.0.99 cannot read an allOf / anyOf grant: the flow fails to load, a combinator override stamp is treated as malformed (the child falls back to its own grants), and an old x-roles parser skips the entry so a combinator deny vanishes | Author the first allOf / anyOf grant only after every pod, and every domain that stamps overrides onto this one, runs a release containing combinators. |
| `file-store-orphans-on-rollback` | >=0.0.100 | open | warning | runtime | The file object is written to the binding before the unit of work commits and before the transition is reserved or accepted, so a unit-of-work rollback after the store, or a 409 (Busy, SubFlow completion window) answered after the store, leaves an unreferenced object in the binding. Nothing in the runtime tracks or collects such objects. | Apply a lifecycle/expiry rule on the bucket or directory behind the binding (use FileStorage:KeyPrefix to scope it); an orphan is harmless to instance data. |
| `file-store-no-delete` | >=0.0.100 | open | warning | runtime | Clearing (null/absent) or replacing an x-storage field never deletes the previous object, and there is no retention or garbage collection: every object ever stored for an instance stays in the binding. | Manage retention in the store itself (lifecycle rules); do not change FileStorage:KeyPrefix after the first write, or stored objects become unreachable. |
| `file-in-task-record` | >=0.0.100 | open | warning | task | Task records are not covered by the x-storage swap: a mapping that puts file bytes (for example a base64 string) into a task request or response stores them in the task record as authored. | Pass the handle (not the content) through mappings and fetch bytes with ScriptBase.GetFileAsync only where the task needs them; avoid echoing bytes into task responses. |
| `file-trusted-payload-cross-domain` | >=0.0.100 | open | warning | instance | The trusted-payload flag does not cross domains: Start/SubProcess trigger tasks, DirectTrigger and proxied SubFlow forwards that target another domain call its public endpoints, so a content-less x-storage reference in such a body is rejected there with 400 Instance:100048 (a handle from this domain's store is not readable by the other domain anyway). | Send content (base64) rather than a handle in cross-domain bodies, or have the owning domain read the file with ScriptBase.GetFileAsync. |
| `file-seed-data-not-offloaded` | >=0.0.100 | open | info | runtime | Instance data appended from a definition's seed data passes no workflow to the write funnel, so x-storage content in seed data is stored inline in the instance data instead of being offloaded. | Do not place x-storage file content in seed data; upload it through a transition after the instance exists. |
| `file-async-proxy-overlapping-revert` | >=0.0.100 | open | low | runtime | Two overlapping async requests proxied through one parent to its active SubFlow: when one forward fails and reverts, the revert can clear the Busy stamp the other request set; the next child notification restores the parent's status. | None needed in normal operation (self-heals on the next child notification); clients should not fire overlapping async transitions at the same parent. |
| `file-missing-object-503` | >=0.0.100 | open | low | runtime | A get of an x-storage object that no longer exists in the store (deleted by a bucket lifecycle rule or by hand) answers 503 Instance:100047 FileStoreUnavailable, indistinguishable from a store outage, because the Dapr binding reports both as an invocation error. | Do not expire objects still referenced by instance data; check the store for the object key (FileStorage:KeyPrefix + file) when a 503 persists for one file only. |
| `file-duplicate-property-names` | >=0.0.100 | open | low | runtime | A payload whose x-storage node repeats a member name (for example two 'content' or 'file' members) is handled inconsistently: the read-only element probe and the mutable node used by the swap do not necessarily see the same occurrence, so the outcome (swap, keep or reject) is not defined. | Send well-formed JSON without duplicate member names; standard JSON serializers never produce them. |

## Security policies

| Id | Scope | Enforced since | Error code | HTTP | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `query-filter-count-and-length-limits` | query | 0.0.1 |  |  | Instance/query filter inputs reject more than InputValidator.MaxFiltersCount filters and any filter string longer than InputValidator.MaxFilterLength. |
| `query-field-name-safety` | query | 0.0.1 |  |  | Filter field paths must satisfy InputValidator.ValidateFieldName: length limits, max dot depth, alphanumeric segments starting with a letter, and rejection of dangerous punctuation/control characters. |
| `query-filter-value-length` | query | 0.0.94 | `filter.valueTooLong` | 400 | InstanceQueryValidator and SQL condition builders enforce InputValidator.MaxValueLength before SQL compilation. |
| `query-includes-json-limits` | query | 0.0.1 |  |  | Includes-filter JSON payloads must be objects bounded by InputValidator MaxIncludesPayloadJsonLength, MaxIncludesPayloadNestingDepth, and MaxIncludesPayloadPropertyCount (including array element counts). |
| `query-json-and-sql-identifier-safety` | query | 0.0.1 |  |  | Arbitrary JSON strings are capped by InputValidator.ValidateJsonLength (same max as filters); JSONB column identifiers must pass InputValidator.ValidateSqlJsonColumnIdentifier (PostgreSQL-safe quoted identifiers). |
| `transition-automatic-trigger-system-actor-only` | transition | 0.0.1 |  |  | ActorAuthorizationSpecification requires ExecutionActor.System for TriggerType.Automatic transitions. |
| `transition-scheduled-trigger-system-actor-only` | transition | 0.0.1 |  |  | ActorAuthorizationSpecification requires ExecutionActor.System for TriggerType.Scheduled transitions. |
| `transition-automatic-chain-depth-limit` | transition | 0.0.1 |  |  | ActorAuthorizationSpecification rejects automatic transitions when TransitionExecutionContext.ChainDepth exceeds 50 (defense in depth alongside the pipeline). |
| `transition-role-grant-evaluation` | transition | 0.0.1 |  |  | TransitionAuthorizationManager evaluates transition RoleGrant lists: any matching DENY denies; otherwise any matching ALLOW permits; empty role grants allow all callers. |
| `roleless-caller-cannot-clear-role-bound-deny` | authorization | 0.0.96 |  |  | A caller with no roles cannot pass a role-bound DENY grant (a static role or a $role. |
| `role-grant-combinators-three-valued-evaluation` | authorization | 0.0.99 |  |  | Grants are evaluated three-valued by the single RoleGrantMatcher (used by RoleGrantEvaluator and EvaluateRolesStatic): a role-bound leaf (static role, $role.) is Unknown for a role-less caller, identity leaves ($InstanceStarter, $PreviousUser, $InstanceBehalfOfStarter, $PreviousBehalfOfUser, $user., $userBehalfOf.) are always Yes/No (No when there is no instance). |
| `queryroles-decided-at-subflow-leaf-only` | authorization | 0.0.99 |  |  | For an instance with an active SubFlow, AuthorizeAppService does not evaluate queryRoles above the deepest active leaf: it only forwards, and the leaf decides (parent-stamped subFlow.overrides.states.<state>.queryRoles, else the leaf state's queryRoles, else the leaf workflow's); there is no AND down the chain, an empty leaf set allows. |
| `transition-predefined-and-dynamic-role-grants` | transition | 0.0.1 |  |  | When an instance is present, TransitionAuthorizationManager resolves $InstanceStarter, $PreviousUser, $InstanceBehalfOfStarter, $PreviousBehalfOfUser against CreatedBy/CreatedByBehalfOf and last completed manual transition; dynamic grants use $.context.* paths compared to actor, subject, or caller role. |
| `schema-field-masking-allow-only-exemption` | authorization | 0.0.99 |  |  | SchemaFieldFilterService applies master-schema x-masking after x-roles pruning on instance GET, instance list, the data function and sync start/transition attributes (IInstanceDataReadService), and on the Get* trigger tasks for the header set the task presents. |
| `schema-field-encryption-at-rest` | data-protection | 0.0.99 |  |  | x-encryption.type 'encrypt': InstanceDataWriteService seals the declared string paths of InstancesData with AES-256-GCM under the instance's own key (AAD bound to scheme, instance and path) after validation; InstanceData.Data is the column as stored and is never decrypted in place (no plaintext member, no materialization interceptor), so no tracking state writes plaintext; decryption only through IInstanceDataProtector.UnprotectAsync (write funnel, read guard, script DecryptAsync of the instance's own path); content and DataHash are ignored after save and detached rows are attached Unchanged. |

| `attribute-index-catalog` | 0.0.94 | query | `AttributeIndexes:Enabled`=false, `AttributeIndexes:DisabledFlows`=[], `AttributeIndexes:CatalogCacheSeconds`=30 | Read-only ready-index routing. |
